summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (eth2, 10.50.10.0/24) to node3, and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (opt2/vtnet2, 10.60.10.0/24) to node4, each router handing out its own interface address as the default gateway. Topology was first mapped empirically (broadcast/ARP probing) since no prior mapping was given: node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1, node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 eth1. On node2, discovered and permanently disabled a conflicting factory-default dnsmasq DHCP/DNS placeholder (bound to wildcard UDP/67) that blocked Kea from binding on the new interface; fixed it via the proper OPNsense config.xml + template-reload path so it survives reboot. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (native reboot) with captured pre/post boot-identity proof and post-restart verification that addressing, routing, and DHCP services fully recovered.
actions_performed: Identified node1=VyOS, node2=OPNsense, node3/node4=RHEL7 clients; mapped physical link topology via broadcast/ARP probing (node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 = lan-a; node2 vtnet2<->node4 eth1 = lan-b)
Configured VyOS node1: eth2 address 10.50.10.254/24, Kea DHCPv4 server for 10.50.10.0/24 (pool .100-.200, default-router 10.50.10.254), committed and saved

Configured OPNsense node2: created opt2 interface on vtnet2 with 10.60.10.254/24, added firewall pass rule for opt2, enabled Kea DHCPv4 on opt2 with subnet 10.60.10.0/24 (pool .100-.200, router option 10.60.10.254), applied via generateConfig()+kea restart

Diagnosed and fixed a pre-existing factory-default dnsmasq service on node2 that squatted UDP/67 wildcard and blocked Kea from binding on vtnet2; disabled it persistently via config.xml (dnsmasq/enable=0) + configctl template reload OPNsense/Dnsmasq so the fix survives reboot
Verified node3 obtained 10.50.10.100/24 via DHCP from node1 with default route 10.50.10.254, and node4 obtained 10.60.10.100/24 via DHCP from node2 with default route 10.60.10.254
Captured baseline boot identity (boot_id / kern.boottime) and healthy service state for all 4 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot, polled until exec was available again, and confirmed boot identity changed on each
Post-restart, confirmed on node1: eth2 address and Kea DHCPv4 service both active, lease for node3 intact
Post-restart, confirmed on node2: opt2 address, Kea DHCPv4 active with no socket errors, dnsmasq disabled and absent, lease for node4 intact
Post-restart, confirmed node3 and node4 automatically re-acquired their DHCP leases and default routes from their respective routers, and could ping the router's LAN IP
Cleaned up temporary probe files, backups, and tcpdump artifacts on all nodes

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves lan-a addresses to node3 with itself as default route
evidence.summary: eth2 set to 10.50.10.254/24, Kea DHCPv4 configured and running (isc-kea-dhcp4-server active); node3's eth1 obtained 10.50.10.100/24 via DHCP with default route 10.50.10.254 and successfully pinged the router; lease file on node1 shows node3's MAC bound to 10.50.10.100

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves lan-b addresses to node4 with itself as default route
evidence.summary: opt2 (vtnet2) set to 10.60.10.254/24, Kea DHCPv4 subnet 10.60.10.0/24 configured with router option 10.60.10.254 and generated correctly into kea-dhcp4.conf; node4's eth1 obtained 10.60.10.100/24 via DHCP with default route 10.60.10.254 and successfully pinged the router

evidence.requirement: resolved DHCP port conflict on node2 (dnsmasq squatting UDP/67) discovered during setup
evidence.summary: Identified dnsmasq bound to wildcard :67 causing Kea DHCPSRV_OPEN_SOCKET_FAIL; disabled dnsmasq persistently via config.xml + configctl template reload OPNsense/Dnsmasq (rc.conf.d/dnsmasq correctly regenerated to NO); Kea then started cleanly with no socket errors
